newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Intertie power limits in place to Nov-Dec.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Intertie power limits in place to Nov-Dec.

text.p: Capacity restraints on major power lines linking the Northwest to California will remain in place through November or December, an executive at the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Thursday.
George Bell, BPA's group vice president for transmission, said studies to determine criteria for safe operation of the Pacific Intertie lines will likely be completed by then.
"We are committed to reliability. The system will be much stronger as a result, although I don't think anyone wanted to see it happen this way," he said.

Southbound power transmissions on the AC segment of the line have been limited to 3,200 megawatts (MW), or 65 percent of its 4,800 MW capacity, since a major power outage hit nine western states on Aug 10.
The DC line was limited to 2,000 MW of its 3,200 MW capacity.
These limits represent maximum usage, and the lines are at times subject to further constraints based on the potential impact of other, smaller line outages, Bell said.

He noted the intertie limits "will remain in effect until studies are completed to establish sufficient 'nomograms' (relationships) for how you will make changes in intertie ratings based on what is going on in the rest of the system, such as equipment outages and flows."
For instance, the volume and direction of flows between Idaho and Bonneville's system are already being taken into account as criteria for safe operation of the system, Bell said.
